note: Every rule is a verbatim quote from a live free page. Nothing here is invented.

rules.quote: Three sessions a week on non-consecutive days, for example Monday, Wednesday and Friday, with 3 sets and 60 to 90 seconds of rest.
3 sets at a hold you can repeat cleanly
Warm-up, 3 sets, 60 to 90 seconds of rest, record actual holds

rules.value: same hold for weeks 1 and 2
rules.quote: Establish repeatable sessions

rules.value: keep bar, grip and assistance the same
rules.quote: Keep the bar, grip and assistance the same.
Same hold, or add about 5 seconds once every set is clean

rules.value: review logged holds; keep settings or change one variable
rules.quote: Look at logged holds. Keep the settings or change one variable.

rules.value: 3 sets at the revised hold
rules.quote: 3 sets at the revised hold

rules.value: return to previous setup if the new one is too demanding
rules.quote: Return to the previous setup if the new one is too demanding.

rules.value: 3 sets at the setup that worked best

rules.value: comfortable 20 to 30 seconds
rules.quote: The 8-week program suits you once you can hold a comfortable 20 to 30 seconds.

rules.value: under 20 to 30 seconds: use the 4-week program
rules.quote: If you cannot yet, start with the 4-week program.

rules.value: four rest days, non-consecutive hang days
rules.quote: A typical week in the 8-week program has three hang sessions on non-consecutive days and four rest days.

rules.value: add a session only if pain free
rules.quote: Add a session only if you stay pain free.

rules.value: step down a second or two before grip gives out; no failure
rules.quote: Step down a second or two before your grip gives out, and do not hang to failure.

rules.value: do not make up extra sets
rules.quote: A missed session does not require making up extra sets.

rules.value: change the plan when a hold is painful or step-down is not controlled
rules.quote: Change the 8-week plan when a hold is painful or when you cannot step down under control.

rules.value: compare supported with supported, unassisted with unassisted
rules.quote: Compare supported hangs with supported hangs and unassisted hangs with unassisted hangs.

rules.value: stop a painful hold; end a set before control goes
rules.quote: Stop a painful hold and end a set before your control goes.

rules.value: 12-week program suits a comfortable hold of 30 seconds or longer
rules.quote: suits a comfortable hold of 30 seconds or longer.

rules.value: 3 sets, 90 seconds rest
rules.quote: Perform your normal 3 sets at Week 3 target times with 90 seconds rest between sets.
Rest stays at 90 seconds between sets.

rules.value: about 5 seconds
rules.quote: The program suits anyone who can hold the bar for about 5 seconds.

rules.value: about 80% of the max test hold
rules.quote: Your baseline hold is about 80% of that number.

rules.value: the hold you can repeat for three clean sets; week 1 target
rules.quote: It is the hold you can repeat for three clean sets and it is your Week 1 target.

rules.value: hang until a second or two before grip gives out
rules.quote: Hang until a second or two before your grip gives out.

rules.value: 3 sets at baseline
rules.quote: Every set uses your baseline hold.
Add 5 seconds to each set compared to your Week 1 times.
Add another 5 seconds per set on top of Week 2.

rules.value: one session in week 3 may use neutral grip
rules.quote: On one session this week swap your overhand grip for a neutral grip

rules.value: sessions 1 and 2 at week 3 targets; session 3 is test day
rules.quote: These sessions maintain volume without draining you before the final test.

rules.value: 2 easy hangs of 10 to 15 seconds
rules.quote: Warm up with a short mobility routine and 2 easy hangs of 10 to 15 seconds each

rules.value: 2 to 3 minutes
rules.quote: Rest 2-3 minutes

rules.value: best controlled hold; step down before grip gives out
rules.quote: Grip the bar and hang for your best controlled hold. Step down a second or two before your grip gives out.

rules.value: 30 seconds or longer; not a fixed outcome
rules.quote: Target: 30 seconds or longer. Test day shows where you are now. It is not a fixed outcome.

rules.value: 2 to 3 seconds short on set 3 is acceptable
rules.quote: Falling 2 to 3 seconds short on the third set is normal and acceptable.

rules.value: repeat current week if missing by more than 5 seconds
rules.quote: Repeat the current week before progressing if you consistently miss by more than 5 seconds.

rules.value: repeat weeks 3 and 4 if test is under 30
rules.quote: Repeat weeks 3 and 4 until you reach 30 if you start lower.

rules.value: under 5 minutes per week for baseline up to 20 seconds
rules.quote: Weekly hang time stays under 5 minutes for a baseline up to 20 seconds.

rules.value: under 5 seconds: regression exercises for 1 to 2 weeks first
rules.quote: Start with the regression exercises in the beginner dead hang guide for 1 to 2 weeks before beginning this program.

rules.value: rest day between sessions
rules.quote: A rest day between sessions is the common starting rule.

rules.value: 2 sessions per week at 3 sets each at 30 seconds
rules.quote: Keep your 30-second hold with 2 sessions per week at 3 sets each.

rules.value: common training practice, not a tested prescription
rules.quote: The doses are common training practice, not a tested prescription.

rules.value: 5 to 10 seconds
rules.quote: Aim for 5-10 seconds on your first real dead hang.

rules.value: 3 sets of 15 seconds with as much help as needed; rest 90 to 120 seconds
rules.quote: 3 sets of 15 seconds with as much help as you need. Rest 90 to 120 seconds between sets.

rules.value: 3 sets of 5 seconds, then add about 5 seconds when every set is clean
rules.quote: For feet-off holds, one common pattern is 3 sets of 5 seconds, then adding about 5 seconds once every set is clean.

rules.value: never hang to failure
rules.quote: Never hang to failure.
rest 90 to 120 seconds between sets and train on non-consecutive days.

rules.value: 5 seconds, roughly once a week, when every set is complete cleanly
rules.quote: Add about 5 seconds to your target hold once you complete every set cleanly, roughly once a week.

rules.value: under 10 minutes
rules.quote: Each session takes less than 10 minutes.

rules.value: add a session only if pain free
rules.quote: Add a session only if you stay pain free, and leave at least one rest day between hard sessions.

rules.value: example only: week 1 target 5-10 seconds per set
rules.quote: 5-10 seconds

rules.value: example only: week 2 target 10-15 seconds per set
rules.quote: 10-15 seconds

rules.value: example only: week 3 target 15-22 seconds per set
rules.quote: 15-22 seconds

rules.value: example only: week 4 target 22-30 seconds per set
rules.quote: 22-30 seconds

rules.quote: The 4-week table is an example of how targets can rise, not a norm.

rules.value: step down before grip gives out
rules.quote: Step down under control before your grip gives out.

rules.value: 3 sets of 15 seconds, 90 seconds rest
rules.quote: Three sets of 15 seconds, with as much assistance as you need to reach 15. Rest 90 seconds between sets.

rules.value: 15 seconds across all 3 sets with minimal assistance
rules.quote: You hold 15 seconds across all 3 sets with minimal assistance.

rules.value: 30-second overhand hang completed 3 times in one session
rules.quote: 30-second overhand dead hang completed 3 times in one session

rules.value: 15 to 30 seconds
rules.quote: Hold for 15 to 30 seconds.

rules.value: 10 to 20 seconds
rules.quote: Hang with fully extended arms for 10 to 20 seconds.

rules.value: record the assist used so tests stay comparable
rules.quote: Record the assist you used so tests stay comparable.

rules.value: ten seconds or fewer to start if cleared to hang
rules.quote: Two physiotherapy academics advise ten seconds or fewer to start if you are cleared to hang.

rules.value: sharp pain, numbness, light-headedness, pinching shoulder
rules.quote: Stop and step down if you notice sharp pain, numbness, light-headedness or a pinching shoulder.

rules.value: use a step or box to reach the bar
rules.quote: Use a step or box to reach the bar safely.

rules.value: chalk helps if sweat, not fatigue, ends the hang
rules.quote: Chalk helps if sweat, not fatigue, ends your hang.

rules.value: common training practice, not a tested prescription
rules.quote: This is common training practice, not a tested prescription.

rules.value: 3 per week, non-consecutive; add a session only if pain free
rules.quote: Start with 3 sessions a week on non-consecutive days and add a session only if you stay pain free

rules.value: 3 sets of 15 seconds, 90 seconds rest
rules.quote: Level 1 uses 3 sets of 15-second holds with as much assistance as you need to reach 15 seconds. Rest 90 seconds between sets.

rules.value: 15 seconds across all 3 sets with minimal assistance
rules.quote: Move to Level 2 when you can hold 15 seconds across all 3 sets with minimal foot or band assistance.

rules.value: 3 sets of 15 to 30 seconds, rest 60 to 90 seconds
rules.quote: Level 2 uses 3 sets of 15 to 30 second holds with 60 to 90 seconds of rest.

rules.value: 5 seconds, roughly once a week
rules.quote: Add about 5 seconds to your target hold once you complete every set cleanly, roughly once a week.

rules.value: 30 seconds for 3 sets with clean form
rules.quote: Move to Level 3 when you can hold 30 seconds for 3 sets with clean form.

rules.value: stop a second or two before grip gives out
rules.quote: Stop a second or two before your grip gives out and step down under control.

rules.value: 3 or 4 sets of 30 to 60 seconds, rest 60 to 90 seconds
rules.quote: Level 3 uses 3 or 4 sets of 30 to 60 second holds with 60 to 90 seconds of rest.

rules.value: 60 seconds for 3 sets
rules.quote: Move to Level 4 when you hold 60 seconds for 3 sets.

rules.value: 60-second hold is a personal milestone, not a published standard
rules.quote: A 60-second hold is a personal milestone on this ladder.

rules.value: 3 or 4 sets of 20 to 45 seconds, rest 60 to 90 seconds
rules.quote: Level 4 uses 3 or 4 sets of 20 to 45 second holds with 60 to 90 seconds of rest.

rules.value: active hang 45 seconds across 3 sets
rules.quote: Move to Level 5 when you hold an active hang for 45 seconds across 3 sets.

rules.value: comfortable pain-free bodyweight hang of about 45 seconds before adding load
rules.quote: Level 5 also needs a comfortable and pain-free bodyweight hang of about 45 seconds before you add load.

rules.value: start 5 to 10 lbs (2 to 5 kg), add about 5 lbs when every set is clean
rules.quote: Start with 5 to 10 lbs (2 to 5 kg) and add about 5 lbs once every set is clean.

rules.value: 3 or 4 sets of 15 to 30 seconds, rest 90 to 120 seconds
rules.quote: Level 5 uses 3 or 4 sets of 15 to 30 second holds with 90 to 120 seconds of rest.

rules.value: controlled two-arm hang of about 60 seconds
rules.quote: Move to Level 6 when you can hold a controlled two-arm hang for about 60 seconds.

rules.value: 2 or 3 sets per arm, rest 2 to 3 minutes
rules.quote: Level 6 uses 2 or 3 sets per arm with 2 to 3 minutes of rest.

rules.value: target hold for 3 consecutive sets in one session
rules.quote: You reach the target hold time for 3 consecutive sets in a single session.

rules.value: no breakdown in arm extension, shoulder position, core engagement or breathing
rules.quote: No breakdown in arm extension, shoulder position, core engagement or breathing during any set.

rules.value: zero sharp, shooting or radiating pain
rules.quote: Zero sharp, shooting or radiating pain in your hands, wrists, elbows or shoulders during or after training.

rules.value: stay at current level or drop back one
rules.quote: If any pain develops, stay at your current level or drop back one level.

rules.value: start at the level matching your current hold
rules.quote: Start at the level that matches your current hold and meet its criteria.

rules.value: weeks are a sample; heavier people often take longer
rules.quote: Timelines vary with bodyweight and training history. Heavier people often take longer at each level.

rules.value: any listed sign ends the hang
rules.quote: Any item below ends the hang.

rules.value: step down under control; do not drop
rules.quote: Step down under control. Do not drop.

rules.value: sit down until it passes
rules.quote: If you feel light-headed or faint, sit down until it passes.

rules.value: do not continue that session
rules.quote: Do not continue that session.

rules.value: seek medical advice if it recurs or persists
rules.quote: Seek medical advice if it recurs or persists.

rules.value: if in doubt, holds of 10 seconds or fewer
rules.quote: If in doubt, start with holds of 10 seconds or fewer

rules.value: stop one or two seconds before grip gives out
rules.quote: Stop one or two seconds before your grip gives out and step down under control.

rules.value: release the bar immediately
rules.quote: Release the bar immediately

rules.value: stop and rest; see a clinician if it persists
rules.quote: Stop and rest; see a clinician if it persists

rules.value: joint pain is a stop sign
rules.quote: Joint pain is your stop sign.

rules.value: see a clinician if it recurs
rules.quote: See a clinician if it happens again, or if tingling or pain lasts after you let go.

rules.value: breathe normally; do not hold your breath
rules.quote: Breathe normally from the start of a hang. Do not hold your breath.

rules.value: lower feet first and step down
rules.quote: Lower yourself feet first and step down.

rules.value: feet 15 to 30 cm (6 to 12 inches) from the ground when starting
rules.quote: Keep your feet 15 to 30 cm (6 to 12 inches) from the ground when starting.

rules.value: rubber mat, carpet or grass
rules.quote: Hang over a rubber mat, carpet or grass.

rules.value: both feet on the ground, remove weight gradually
rules.quote: Start with both feet on the ground and remove weight gradually by bending your knees.

rules.value: short holds of 5 to 10 seconds, increase gradually
rules.quote: Start with short holds of 5 to 10 seconds and increase gradually.

rules.value: ask a clinician first with shoulder hypermobility or instability
rules.quote: Ask a physical therapist or doctor before hanging if you have shoulder hypermobility or instability.

rules.value: cut volume to about half for the first two weeks back
rules.quote: A cautious option is to cut your training volume to about half for the first two weeks back

rules.value: 50% of pre-break max hold, 2 sets, 3 sessions
rules.quote: 50% of pre-break max hold, 2 sets per session, 3 sessions

rules.value: 65% of pre-break max hold, 3 sets, 3 sessions
rules.quote: 65% of pre-break max hold, 3 sets per session, 3 sessions

rules.value: 80% of pre-break max hold, 3 to 4 sets, 3 sessions with a rest day between
rules.quote: 80% of pre-break max hold, 3 to 4 sets per session, 3 sessions with a rest day between

rules.value: resume normal programming if pain free
rules.quote: Resume normal programming if you stayed pain free

rules.value: return plan is practical guidance, not trial-tested
rules.quote: Example Return Plan (Practical Guidance, Not Trial-Tested)

rules.value: about 5 seconds once every set is clean, roughly weekly
rules.quote: Add about 5 seconds once every set is clean, roughly weekly

rules.value: at least one rest day between hard sessions
rules.quote: Leave at least one rest day between hard sessions.

rules.value: lighter week about every fourth week (convention, not a tested rule)
rules.quote: A lighter week about every fourth week is a common coaching convention and not a tested rule.

rules.value: 2 to 3 minutes of arm circles, wrist circles, band pull-aparts, one or two easy hangs
rules.quote: Spend 2 to 3 minutes on arm circles, wrist circles, band pull-aparts and one or two short easy hangs.

rules.value: stop one or two seconds before grip gives out; do not hang to failure or drop
rules.quote: Stop one or two seconds before your grip gives out and step down under control. Do not hang to failure or drop from the bar.

rules.value: count breaths during the first 10 seconds
rules.quote: Counting your breaths during the first 10 seconds of each hang helps you notice.

rules.value: brace core, squeeze glutes, keep legs together
rules.quote: Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, keep your legs together

rules.value: straighten the arms fully at the start of every hang
rules.quote: Straighten the arms fully at the start of every hang

rules.value: hands about shoulder width; log it
rules.quote: Keep hands about shoulder width and log it

rules.value: decide passive or active before grabbing the bar
rules.quote: Decide passive or active before you grab the bar

rules.value: bare hands for grip work; straps for hand injury
rules.quote: Use bare hands for grip work; keep straps for hand injury

rules.value: a shorter hang with good form beats a longer hang with poor form
rules.quote: A shorter hang with good form beats a longer hang with poor form.

rules.value: start lighter and keep feet on a box if form breaks down
rules.quote: Start lighter if your form breaks down. Keep your feet on a box to take part of your weight until you can hold correct position.
